fine_trace.note: Attacker-controlled ELF header field: the packed input declares e_phnum == 1, so the parser prepares a single Elf64_Phdr and never validates that at least 2 program headers exist (the fix d3e780d6 adds exactly this check in canUnpack).
file_image is allocated with len = sz_phdrs + e_phoff = (e_phnum*56) + 64 = 120 bytes for e_phnum==1; this MemBuffer is the allocation that the later OOB read runs past.
phdri is bounded to exactly one Elf64_Phdr inside the 120-byte file_image; phdri[1] therefore lies at offset 120, immediately past the end of the buffer.

checkEhdr only rejects e_phnum < 1; the missing e_phnum >= 2 validation (added later by fix d3e780d6 as 'if (get_te16(&ehdri.e_phnum) < 2) throwCantUnpack("e_phnum must be >= 2")') lets the e_phnum==1 packed file be accepted and proceed to unpack(), where phdri[1] is dereferenced without any bound check.
unpack() re-reads the same attacker-controlled count: c_phnum == 1, so the only program header available is phdri[0].
The attacker sets phdri[0].p_filesz == 0x1000, so the first operand of the C_BASE-style detection evaluates true and the second operand (&phdri[1].p_offset) is evaluated.

Sink: get_te64 -> N_BELE_RTP::LEPolicy::get64 -> get_le64 -> get_ne64 reads 8 bytes at file_image+64+56+8 = file_image+128, i.e. 8 bytes past the 120-byte file_image MemBuffer: ASan reports heap-buffer-overflow READ 8 in PackLinuxElf64::unpack.
